question: When did the women discover that Jesus's body was missing?
summary: Luke 24:2-4 and John 20:1-2 have the women (or Mary Magdalene) discover the body is missing *before* they encounter any angelic figure — they enter, find the body gone, and only then do the angels appear (Luke) or Mary runs to tell Peter (John). Matthew 28:5-6 and Mark 16:5-6 have the women see the angel/young man *first*, and only learn from him that the body is gone. Two gospels: discovery, then angel. Two gospels: angel, then announcement.

reconcile.connective: Gill harmonizes the order by reading Luke's women as already prompted by Matthew's angel before they themselves find the tomb empty.

discrepancy.connective: Bart Ehrman treats the empty-tomb accounts' differing order of discovery and angelic announcement as one of the Gospels' clearest, unharmonizable contradictions.

pd_work.resource: John Haley, An Examination of the Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible (1874)
pd_work.author: John Haley
pd_work.note: Haley's "Historical Discrepancies" section (pp. 327-329, under the heading "Christ's resurrection, — certain narratives. Different account of it," setting Matt. 28:1-10 and Mark 16:1-14 against Luke 24:1-12 and John 20:1-18) gives a full sequenced harmony, quoting Robinson: the angel has already descended and sat on the stone before the women arrive; they then enter, find the body gone, and are perplexed; and only afterward do two angels appear and speak — directly addressing the order in which discovery and angelic announcement occur across the four accounts.

link.title: GotQuestions: Can the various resurrection accounts from the four Gospels be harmonized?
link.note: Presents a single sequenced harmony of the empty-tomb morning (angel descends and rolls the stone away, then the women arrive and find it empty) that resolves the ordering tension, though it does not flag the tension by name.

excerpts.attribution: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible (1746-63)
excerpts.excerpt_text: And they entered in,.... To the sepulchre, being invited, encouraged, and led on by the angel that sat upon the stone; … and found not the body of the Lord Jesus …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Gill addresses the order tension directly: an angel (Matthew's, already seated on the stone) is already present and prompting the women before they themselves discover the tomb is empty, reconciling Luke's later-order account with Matthew's angel-first sequence.
